name: Porto
tagline: Port cellars and a riverside of tiles
summary: Keep Porto compact: the Ribeira riverside and bridge, the tiled churches uptown, and the port lodges across the river in Gaia. Add a Douro Valley day for vineyards.
seasonNote: Atlantic rain is common from November to March; summer is warm rather than hot.
arrival: Metro line E runs from the airport to Trindade in about 30 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk, but expect hills; the metro, funicular and Gaia cable car save the steepest climbs.
cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; some small tascas prefer cash.
foodTip: Share a francesinha, try tripas or grilled fish in Matosinhos, and taste tawny against ruby port.
buyTip: Port bought at the lodges, tinned fish, and cork or filigree from named makers.

connections.note: From Campanhã station; book ahead for the best fares.
Air time only; add airport transfers.

items.name: Ribeira and Dom Luís I Bridge
items.summary: A double-deck iron bridge over the Douro with the old riverside quarter at its foot.
items.expect: Crowds on the quay and a shared upper deck with metro trains.
items.tip: Cross the top deck at sunset and come back along the lower one.
